why: tools/seams.mjs measures whether two strings match. That is a real gate and it caught real
holes, but it cannot tell a closed seam from a closed-looking one: once a name has an emitter
and a listener it is never examined again. P36 round 2 satisfied it completely — world:resonance
emitted, heard, and lighting four real PointLights — while the shipped game changed 0 of 518,400
pixels, because every one of those lights hung in clear air with no surface inside its falloff.
That is the wave's own dominant failure mode reproduced one level up, inside the tool built to
detect it.
So this file is the second half of the gate. `baseline.oneEnded` is every signal name the audit
has ever reported with only one end during this wave; any of those that now has BOTH ends is a
newly-closed seam, and a newly-closed seam has to say what closing it was worth. The measurement
shape is fixed on purpose (see `kind` below): halt the realtime loop, render twice at
k.advance(0) so nothing in the world integrates between reads, and diff the drawing buffer with
the thing under test present and absent. Control is the two-render noise floor; if it is not
exactly 0 the instrument cannot resolve a single code value and the treatment number means
nothing.
kind:
pixels    a zero-time A/B on the shipped path. Requires control === 0 and treatment > 0.
state     a zero-time observable state delta on the shipped path, for seams that legitimately
move no pixels. Requires before !== after and a probe path that a reviewer can read.
hygiene   the seam changes no behaviour at all — a declared channel replacing a duck-typed
lookup, say. Legitimate, but it must NOT be counted as a player-visible closure, and
it must say what the two paths measured identically.
blindspot the name was never actually one-ended: the audit's own regex could not see the
listener. Requires the listener's file:line, and is a finding about the tool.
owed      closed by a piece that has not priced it yet. Names the owner. Reported on every run
so it cannot go quiet, in the same spirit as ⟨pending Pnn⟩ in the vocabulary.

note: Round 2 closed the string pairing and measured 0. The emitter sent the ink's own position and
every claim stands 10.7-21.2 m above the ground, so all four accents hung in air: 0 of 26
sphere casts from any accent found a surface inside its falloff. Round 3 sends the claim's
socket instead — collision.groundAt under the ink, lifted 1 m — and the same cast now finds
world at 0.73-0.95 m from every accent, 9-12 directions of 26. The 412 px are one accent
(leaf9-mark, whose socket lands 0.95 m from a drawn boulder); the three over open flat ground
are worth under a code value each at 15 m, which is what §5.4's intensity cap buys on a
horizontal plane — measured directly in review/measure/P36-r3-sweep.mjs.
On the gameplay path (review/measure/P36-r3-play.mjs) the same A/B reads 366 px at spawn and
0 px after E, because pressing E stands the four claims down and leaves one teaching claim
whose socket is on that same open ground. The seam is still demonstrably live there, as a
state delta rather than a pixel one: probe("lighting").accents.registered goes 4 → 1 → 2 as
world:resonance retires three accents and registers the teaching claim's.

note: The rig emits camera:probe 1123 times in eight seconds and nothing answered; boot/30-locomotion.js
now answers it from CollisionWorld.sphereCast. But _castFree already fell through to
kernel.get('collision').sphereCast — the same method — so the boom stands in exactly the same

Worth doing and worth nothing in pixels: it must not be counted as a player-visible closure.
